fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Missing delineated crossings and accessible ramps at ramp terminals, vegetation-limited sight lines, substandard unsigned mid-block four-lane crossing, and a prior pedestrian fatality are substantive preliminary-design-stage safety issues squarely within FHWA interchange/pedestrian audit scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal mechanism and treatment duty are supported by verbatim quotes (EV-US-030 separation failure, EV-US-032 signing/crosswalk requirement), and the site-specific facts (no crosswalks/ramps, vegetation, non-compliant signage, fatal collision) are attributed to recorded sample-report observations, satisfying the grounding rule.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern under FHWA guidance; MUTCD and ADA references function as design-currency criteria inside the safety narrative without converting the item into a formal compliance determination.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific, staged, and actionable (immediate MUTCD signage, ADA ramps/crosswalks in current design, future signalized ramp crossings, relocation to Derby Shoppes signal with sidewalk extension) and avoids a null disposition.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the directly exposed vulnerable road user group with their exposure mechanisms analyzed, and driver attention diversion through the crossing area is also addressed.

justifications.substance: Undefined lane drop with abrupt striping termination, absent advance warning, and observed late merges at an on-ramp mouth create a genuine driver-expectancy/conflict mechanism between merging traffic and ramp-exiting left-turners — a core preliminary-design RSA issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is directly anchored by the verbatim EV-US-033 quote on abrupt striping end and absent signage, with observed merge behavior recorded in Safety Issue #2 and the inferential collision mechanism explicitly flagged as inference rather than evidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern about expectancy and decision load rather than a compliance claim; the EV-US-023 FHWA scope quote is applied appropriately, and pedestrian impacts are cleanly partitioned to the separate finding instead of being conflated.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable (advance merge signage and markings ahead of the on-ramp) and adds a viable preliminary-design alternative — extending two lanes past the ramp with its mandatory-right-turn trade-off signed in advance — carried into ongoing reconstruction.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU applicability is explicitly addressed: pedestrian exposure at the mid-block crosswalk is acknowledged but correctly deferred to JB-GF12-001, with this finding scoped to drivers because its conflict mechanism is vehicle-to-vehicle.
